title: crypto2dev_fd_release: mutex held across memzero_explicit of state struct
description: In crypto2dev_fd_release(), the cleanup sequence is: mutex_lock(&state->lock), do cleanup (sess_free, module_put, outbuf free), mutex_unlock(&state->lock), then memzero_explicit(state, sizeof(*state)), then kfree(state). The memzero_explicit(state) call zeroes the mutex itself (state->lock is at offset 0 of the struct). This is a use-after-unlock of the mutex object: memzero_explicit writes to state->lock after mutex_unlock. On some mutex implementations (e.g. PREEMPT_RT futex-based mutexes) the mutex struct may have kernel-managed waitqueue state. Writing zeros over it after unlock is undefined behavior if any other thread is concurrently blocked on mutex_lock(&state->lock). However: release() is called from the VFS when the file's refcount hits zero. At that point, no other thread can hold a file descriptor reference to this file, so no other thread can be in an ioctl/read/write that holds or waits on state->lock. The only exception would be if a DO_SIGN/DO_VERIFY/DO_AGREE has a reference via fget() to this fd as the key fd, and is concurrently executing. In that case: the key operation holds key_state->lock, not state->lock. fget() takes a file reference, preventing release() from being called. So memzero after unlock is safe here because no concurrent access is possible at release time. No actual bug — checking for correctness. Closing.
